definition: Sentencing economics: the severity of punishment does not depend entirely on the severity of the crime, but is dually modulated by identity/background (inside or outside the establishment) and political need (whether stability is affected)
core_finding: Kui Wood Wolf (seizing a princess + cannibalism) is merely punished with tending the furnace, while the Jing River Dragon King (reducing the rainfall) is beheaded — same crime, different punishment: sentencing is severely imbalanced

sentencing_cases.case_name: Jing River Dragon King · altered the rainfall quota
sentencing_cases.identity: Water-clan dragon deity · Heavenly Court establishment
sentencing_cases.crime: Violated the Jade Emperor's edict · reduced the rainfall (skimming the rain quota)
sentencing_cases.actual_sentence: Beheaded · Wei Zheng supervised the execution
sentencing_cases.aggravating_factors: Violated the Jade Emperor's direct edict · deemed 'defiance of the decree'
sentencing_cases.political_context: The Jade Emperor's need to assert authority · kill one to warn a hundred
sentencing_cases.disparity_reason: Political need outweighs crime severity · the 'defiance' nature dictates heavy punishment

sentencing_cases.case_name: Kui Wood Wolf · seized a princess + cannibalism
sentencing_cases.criminal: Kui Wood Wolf (the Yellow Robe Monster)
sentencing_cases.identity: One of the Twenty-Eight Constellations · senior Heavenly Court establishment
sentencing_cases.crime: Held Princess Baihuaxiu for 13 years + ate palace maids + cannibalized countless people
sentencing_cases.actual_sentence: Demoted to tending the furnace in Tushita Palace · kept his salary and post
sentencing_cases.mitigating_factors: Constellation establishment · senior Heavenly Court deity-general
sentencing_cases.political_context: The Heavenly Court protects its own · constellation establishment takes priority
sentencing_cases.disparity_reason: Protected by senior establishment · the crime is grave but gets 'internal handling'

sentencing_cases.identity: Heavenly Court marshal · senior military commander
sentencing_cases.crime: Molested Chang'e · lost control while drunk
sentencing_cases.actual_sentence: Banished to the mortal realm · mistakenly reborn in a sow's womb
sentencing_cases.mitigating_factors: Marshal establishment · but the impact was severe
sentencing_cases.political_context: Chang'e is a Heavenly Court 'image project' · must be heavily punished
sentencing_cases.disparity_reason: Harmed the 'image project' · must be heavily punished · but the marshal identity was retained

sentencing_cases.case_name: Sha Wujing · shattered the glazed cup
sentencing_cases.identity: Heavenly Court grand general · senior military commander
sentencing_cases.crime: Shattered the glazed cup · breach of etiquette
sentencing_cases.actual_sentence: Banished to the mortal realm · flying swords pierce his chest once every seven days
sentencing_cases.mitigating_factors: None · 'breach of etiquette' was deemed grave dereliction
sentencing_cases.aggravating_factors: Breach of etiquette at the Peach Banquet · harmed the Heavenly Court's dignity
sentencing_cases.political_context: The Peach Banquet is a Heavenly Court 'ritual project' · must be strictly punished
sentencing_cases.disparity_reason: Harmed the 'ritual project' · punishment disproportionate to the crime

sentencing_cases.case_name: Sun Wukong · wreaked havoc in the Heavenly Palace
sentencing_cases.identity: Unaffiliated · self-styled Great Sage Equal to Heaven
sentencing_cases.crime: Wreaked havoc in the Heavenly Palace · vandalized the Peach Orchard + stole immortality pills + ransacked the Heavenly Court
sentencing_cases.actual_sentence: Pinned under Five Elements Mountain for 500 years
sentencing_cases.aggravating_factors: Unaffiliated · disrupted the Heavenly Court's order
sentencing_cases.political_context: The Heavenly Court asserts authority + suppresses rebellion · must be heavily punished
sentencing_cases.disparity_reason: The punishment is reasonable, but the 'unaffiliated' identity made it irrevocable

sentencing_cases.case_name: Green Ox Spirit · descended to earth and ate people
sentencing_cases.crime: Descended to earth for 7 years + cannibalized countless people + trapped the gods' weapons
sentencing_cases.actual_sentence: Reclaimed by its original owner · no punishment
sentencing_cases.political_context: Laozi holds an exalted position · the Heavenly Court finds it inconvenient to intervene
sentencing_cases.disparity_reason: The 'immortal property' identity grants full immunity · the most severe sentencing imbalance

sentencing_cases.case_name: Golden-Winged Great Peng · devoured the Lion Camel Kingdom
sentencing_cases.identity: Uncle of the Tathāgata Buddha · top Vulture Peak establishment
sentencing_cases.crime: Devoured an entire city's people in the Lion Camel Kingdom + the whole country
sentencing_cases.actual_sentence: Reclaimed by its original owner · appointed 'Vulture Peak Dharma Protector'
sentencing_cases.mitigating_factors: Uncle of the Tathāgata · 'uncle of the Buddha' identity
sentencing_cases.political_context: The Tathāgata protects his own + uncle identity
sentencing_cases.disparity_reason: The gravest crime, the lightest punishment · the 'uncle of the Buddha' identity grants complete immunity · and even earns a title

sentencing_cases.case_name: Yellow Robe Monster · descended to earth for 13 years
sentencing_cases.identity: One of the Twenty-Eight Constellations · senior Heavenly Court establishment
sentencing_cases.crime: Descended to earth for 13 years + seized a princess + cannibalism

sentencing_cases.disparity_reason: Senior establishment + the predestined-bond explanation · complete immunity

disparity_analysis.disparity_pattern: Establishment identity > political need > crime severity · sentencing severely imbalanced

sentencing_insights: Heavenly Court sentencing is severely imbalanced: the correlation between crime_severity and sentence_severity is only 0.3
Establishment identity is the most important sentencing factor: 'unaffiliated' demons are uniformly exterminated
Political need comes second: the crime of defying an edict and harming the 'image project' · must be heavily punished
Crime severity matters least: the Great Peng that devoured a country's people goes unpunished · Wukong, who stole immortality pills, is sentenced to 500 years
The essence of sentencing economics: 'protect one's own · eliminate outsiders' · not judicial fairness
The Journey to the West world's justice is entirely 'status-based justice' · not 'punishment proportionate to the crime'
